messages:
Alex: quick heads-up — canary v2-quant is showing a 3x increase in token tail latency on the /chat/completions route vs baseline :warning:
Maria: link? which panel/metric exactly? :mag:
Alex: dashboard -> Model Compare / v2-quant vs v2-fp16, time range 10:30–11:00 UTC. Metric: token_latency_ms_p99 by route
Alex: snapshot of the table we pulled:
```
  route             | model      | p50  | p90  | p99
  /chat/completions | v2-fp16    | 12ms | 28ms | 55ms
  /chat/completions | v2-quant   | 13ms | 35ms | 170ms
  /embeddings       | v2-quant   | 8ms  | 12ms | 15ms
```
Kevin: interesting — p99 spike only on /chat/completions. That implies long sequences + KV behavior or kernel fallback for attention windows. I dug into the kernel selection log:
```
[11:05:14] select_kernel: model=v2-quant, seq_len=1024, chosen_kernel=attn_fast_fp4
[11:05:14] fallback: attn_fast_fp4 -> attn_generic due to missing specialized_stride
[11:05:14] kernel_init_swap: memcpy 120us, kernel_launch_wait 230us
```
Kevin: when fallback happens we see extra memcpy + different shared-memory layout causing a token hotspot for later steps.
Nina: also saw increased KV cache evictions during same window. Eviction log: `kv_evictions: 48/min` vs normal `3/min`. Might be batch alignment issue.
Nina: probable interaction = adaptive batching schedules mixed short+long sequences -> tiny batches hit max_delay -> cause many partial KV entries and then eviction churn.
Maria: can we correlate batch size histogram with the p99 spikes? Perf-bot, do we have any recent profiling traces?
perf-bot: auto-report attached: trace_id=trace-20260318-1106, flame: https://perf.internal/traces/trace-20260318-1106 
perf-bot: top spans: `kv_lookup` (p99=85ms), `kv_eviction` (p99=60ms), `kernel_switch_overhead` (p99=120us)
Alex: thanks. I ran a quick adhoc query on batching bins: `sum by(batch_size) (rate(requests_bucket[5m]))` shows a big bump in batch_size=1 and batch_size=2 at the same time as p99 spike.
Kevin: that matches the kernel fallback behavior — small batches with long seqs sometimes trigger generic kernel which is slower per-token on tail.
Nina: immediate mitigation candidate: bump min_batch_size to 2 for that canary group and increase KV cache capacity for canary to avoid eviction churn. Proposed config patch: 
```
{"route":"/chat/completions","model":"v2-quant","batching":{"min_batch_size":2,"max_delay_ms":6,"heuristic":"adaptive_seq"},"kv_cache":{"capacity_mb":512}}
```
Maria: can we A/B test the change? push to canary subset (10%) and compare p99 and kv_evictions over 30m window.
Alex: yes. I'll create a rollout with canary=10% applying that config. Deploy-bot, request canary rollout?
deploy-bot: canary rollout created: id=rollout-20260318-011, subset=10%, target_label=v2-quant, config_ref=cfg-789, started at 11:12 UTC :rocket:
Kevin: also logging action item to improve kernel selection heuristic: if seq_len > 512 and batch_size <=2, prefer attn_generic optimized path or pre-warm specialized_stride to avoid memcpy fallback. Filed PERF-324.
Nina: filing KV tuning ticket too: PERF-325 — plumb dynamic cache sizing per-canary and tune eviction threshold.
Maria: good. Schedule a follow-up check at 11:45 UTC to compare panels. If p99 drops and kv_evictions fall, we promote change; otherwise rollback.
Alex: thanks team — quick checklist: 1) rollout is running, 2) we're tracking p99 token latency and kv_evictions, 3) perf traces are being captured (trace id above). Ping here with 11:45 numbers. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Kevin: noted. I also exported a short flame sample for the worst trace to the ticket.
perf-bot: alert cleared for high error rate, still tracking latency regression.
deploy-bot: if rollback needed say `rollback rollout-20260318-011` and I'll execute.
Maria: copying plan into the canary incident thread. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
